title: QuadCond prediction record, version 1
description: One record per queried sequence. Frozen at v0.4.2, extended compatibly at v0.4.3 (added `refused` / `refusal_reason`, no field removed): fields may be ADDED in a v1.x release, and a field may never be removed, renamed, or have its meaning changed without incrementing the major version in schema_version. A consumer that reads this document may rely on every required field below existing with the stated meaning for the life of schema 1.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of THIS document's shape, not of the model or the atlas. Model identity lives in model_version; atlas identity in atlas_fingerprint.

atlas_fingerprint.description: Content fingerprint of the atlas the heads were trained on. Two predictions with the same model_version and the same atlas_fingerprint are reproducible against each other.

condition.description: Human-readable buffer label. Display only -- parse condition_detail instead.

condition_imputed_fields.description: Every condition field the caller did not supply, which therefore fell back to a reference default. A number computed under an imputed buffer is not a prediction under a measured one. NEVER omit this when reproducing a record.

evidence.description: Nearest measured atlas records, when an atlas was attached.

claim.description: What this head is allowed to claim, in prose. See docs/CLAIMS.md.

has_experimental_observation.description: Was ANYTHING measured upstream of this label? True for a CUT&Tag proxy as well as for a melting curve. Does not license a folding claim on its own.

target_semantics.description: What the label IS. biophysical = a physical measurement of the structure this head predicts. genomic_proxy = antibody occupancy at a locus, never P(folds). derived = computed from sequence. predicted = another model's output.

biophysically_grounded.description: The ONLY field that licenses a folding or stability claim. Equivalent to target_semantics == 'biophysical'. v0.4.0 shipped a single collapsed field here and it described a proxy head as measurement-grounded; that is why there are three.

calibration_scope.description: The task the reported ECE/Brier/interval was measured on. A calibrated number is calibrated for THIS task and no other.

in_domain.description: False means the query falls outside what this head was trained on. A value may still be present; it is an extrapolation and must not be displayed as a prediction without the warnings beside it. For the stronger case where there is no value at all, see `refused`.

refused.description: This head declined to answer; no value was emitted.

value.description: regression heads only, in the head's own units (degrees C for tm, pH units for ph_t). ABSENT when `refused` is true — do not default it.

interval.description: [low, high] in the head's own units. An OOF-residual interval, NOT a conformal guarantee: the half-width is an out-of-fold residual quantile. The coverage that survives a group split is reported separately in the model card, and is lower than the nominal level.

interval_nominal_level.description: The level the half-width was fitted at. Nominal -- see interval_note for what it actually covers.

refused.description: True when this head declined to answer. A refused head emits NO value, interval or folded fraction — the keys are absent, not null. Distinct from applicability.in_domain=false, which means a value exists and is an extrapolation.
